Petitioner/Appellant(s) Through: Mr. Kaiser Ali, Advocate V/s Union of India and others ... Respondent(s) Through: Mr. T. M. Shamsi, Dsgi with Ms. Yaseema Jan, Advocate Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rahul Bharti, Judge Order
texts.facts: A misplaced and/or undeserving equity extended at some point of time in the past, be it by default or design, in favour of a person with respect to use of State's property/asset cannot be taken to be a matter of use for all time to come in the field of public administration concerning the administration and allotment of state property/assets. 2. The petitioners, through the medium of this writ petition, are literally seeking a perpetual extension of a misplaced equity which was once shown individually in their favour at some point of time in past with respect to the use and occupation of the shop-spaces in STC BSF Campus Humhama, Srinagar, and for that are seeking this court, under article 226 of the Constitution of India, to issue writ of certiorari, mandamus and prohibition so as to checkmate the respondents from going ahead with intended public auction exercise for the shops housed in the STC BSF Complex Humhama Srinagar. 3. Border Security Force, BSF, has a campus at Humhama, Srinagar which is a Subsidiary Training Centre (STC) housing BSF trainees/personnel and officers on regular basis. 5. The petitioners, who are 14 in numbers, joined together to institute the present writ petition filed on 09/01/2018 bearing the status and claim of being in use and occupation of the shops in the said BSF STC Campus, Humhama, and with a purported common cause of action emanating from an issuance of a tender notice No. Prov/Tender-Shop/STC-KMR/2017/19226-35 dated 30/12/2017 by the office of the IG, STC, BSF Kashmir, Srinagar, for the purpose of public auction for renting out the civil shops in the said shopping complex of STC BSF Campus, Humhama for a period of 11 months from the date of issue of allotment order or signing the agreement which everbeing earlier. In terms of the said tender notice, all the shops available in the shopping complex of STC BSF Campus Humhama were meant to be put to public auction in order to fetch highest rent bidders. 6. The petitioners, being in purported use and occupation of some of the shops in the said STC BSF Campus Humhama, reckoned said tender notice to be prejudicial to their purported entitlement to stay in use and occupation of the respective shops held by them and therefore came forward to lay the present petition asking therein in the following reliefs: "(i) Issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of Certiorari in favour of petitioners and against the respondents by quashing the impugned tender notice dated 30.12.2017 forming Annexure G to the writ petition. (ii) Issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of Prohibition Prohibiting the respondents from giving any effect to the impugned tender notice dated 30.12.2017 unless and until decision is not taken upon the representation submitted by them forming part of this writ petition and also unless and until proper procedure and law is not followed by them. (iii) Issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of Mandamus, commanding the respondent to allow the petitioners to run their shops allotted to them for conducting their respective businesses without taking recourse of impugned tender notice and also accept the future rentals from the petitioners as have been accepted by the respondents as on today as reflected in the annexure annexed with the writ petition. (iv) Issue a Writ, Order or Direction in the nature of Mandamus, commanding the respondents to adhere to the promise extended to the petitioners by them while Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/ 2 issuing the allotment orders and also while accepting the one-time rental dues from the petitioners for the period for which no rentals were fixed as reflected in Annexure B and also produce whole record pertaining to the process initiated by them while issuing the impugned tender notice whether the law governing the field and also whether the already promise extended to the petitioners has been strictly followed or not before this Hon'ble court for its onwards consideration and appropriate orders. (v) The Hon'ble Court may pass any other order or direction, which it deems just and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case." 7.
texts.arguments: 43 Thus, the petitioners intend to exploit the very fact that somehow their chance coming into use and occupation of the shops even if before 2010 at the STC BSF Campus for doing the business thereat shall now result into a permanence of their respective business establishment just by demand of 10% hike in rental charges and letting them to stay in the shops on perpetual basis. This expectation of the petitioners is misconceived firstly there is no factual basis set up for this expectation to show its basis and secondly article 14 of the Constitution of India binds the respondents to deal and handle the State's largesse and assets in a fair and open manner even in the matter of its allotments by public competitive auction. To accede to the petitioners' plea would be to issue a writ running contrary to the mandate of article 14 of the Constitution of India. By attributing their participation to auction process held in January 2017 to be under a purported impression and understanding the petitioners are meaning to exploit their self-entertained wrong and misconceived impression and expectation that their one time participation in the auction Shahbaz Sultan And Others vs Union Of India And Others on 3 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190770392/ 11 exercise with respect to the shops in reference would earn in their favour a lifelong allotment. Even if any official/authority of the and at the end of the BSF would have ever extended any such assurance or promise from his end to the petitioners still that would not have meant to be binding to the successors-in-office who are to act and conduct the office and authority in accordance with law with respect to the allotment of the shops.
